info.name: DB Contest — Core API
info.description:
Auth + account management endpoints for the DB Contest Core API (step 1 & 2 of the architecture plan). Sessions are stored server-side and carried in an HttpOnly cookie set by /auth/login — Postman's cookie jar handles it automatically once you run Login inside this collection.

Folders:
- Auth — login, current session, logout, own password change
- Users (admin) — account management, requires `users.manage`
- Operational — health/readiness/metrics on the internal listener (not exposed publicly in production)

Run order for a fresh environment: Auth ▸ Login (bootstrap account) → any Users request → Auth ▸ Logout.

item.name: Auth
item.description: Unauthenticated: Login. Authenticated (session cookie required): Me, Logout, Change password.

request.description:
Authenticates and starts a server-side session. The session token is never returned in the body — it is set as an HttpOnly cookie, which Postman stores and replays automatically on every later request in this collection.

Unknown login and wrong password are indistinguishable (both 401 invalid_credentials) and cost the same time, by design — see docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §7.2.

Responses:
- 200 — `{ user, must_change_password }`. If `must_change_password` is true, every endpoint except /auth/password, /auth/logout and /auth/me will answer 403 `password_change_required` until you call Change password.
- 401 `invalid_credentials`
- 403 `account_blocked`
- 429 `too_many_attempts` — 10/15min per account, 30/15min per address

exec: pm.test('response has user and must_change_password', function () {

request.description:
Replaces the caller's own password. Requires the current password (proof of possession — stops a borrowed unlocked browser from being a permanent takeover). Policy: at least 12 characters, must differ from the current password.

This is the one endpoint reachable while `must_change_password` is still true — it's how a one-time password gets replaced on first sign-in.

Every other session on the account is retired as part of this call, and so is this one: the response clears the session cookie, so log in again with the new password afterwards.

Responses:
- 204 — no body
- 400 `wrong_password` / `weak_password` / `same_password`
- 401 `unauthenticated`

Describes the signed-in account and the exact permission codes its roles grant — useful for building UI that hides what the account may not do.

Responses:
- 200 — `{ id, login, permissions: string[] }`
- 401 `unauthenticated`

Ends the session server-side (not just the cookie) and clears the cookie. Calling it with no session, or twice, is not an error — logging out with a stale cookie is a normal thing for a browser to do.

Responses:
- 204 — no body

item.name: Users (admin)
item.description: Account management. Every route here requires the `users.manage` permission — an installation-wide grant, not scoped to any contest. Run Auth ▸ Login first.

query.description: Matches login, full name or email (case-insensitive substring).

request.description:
Paged account listing.

Responses:
- 200 — `{ items: UserResponse[], total: number }` — `total` counts every match, not just the returned page
- 401 `unauthenticated`
- 403 `forbidden`

Creates an account with a server-generated one-time password. The account is flagged so the first sign-in must replace it — see Auth ▸ Change password.

`roles` are global role codes (`student`, `organizer`, `admin`); omit for a student with no elevated role.

Responses:
- 201 — `{ user, one_time_password }` — the password is shown exactly once and is never retrievable again; a lost one is reset via Users ▸ Reset password
- 400 — malformed body
- 409 `login_taken` / `email_taken`

Changes the descriptive fields only — not status, roles or password.

Responses:
- 204 — no body
- 400 — empty full name / `invalid_user_id`
- 404 `not_found`

Denies access and retires every session the account currently holds — blocking takes effect immediately, not at the next login or whenever an open tab's session happens to expire.

An administrator cannot block their own account (guards against locking yourself out).

Responses:
- 204 — no body
- 400 `cannot_act_on_self`
- 404 `not_found`

Restores access. Sessions retired by the block stay retired — the account signs in again.

Responses:
- 204 — no body
- 404 `not_found`

Issues a fresh one-time password for an account the user can no longer reach, and retires their sessions. Same flag as account creation: the next sign-in must replace it.

Responses:
- 200 — `{ one_time_password }`
- 404 `not_found`

Sets the account's global roles to exactly this set (not a merge). Retires the account's sessions, so a demotion bites on the next request rather than at the next login.

Responses:
- 204 — no body
- 400 — unknown role code / `invalid_user_id`
- 404 `not_found`

item.name: Operational
item.description: Served on the internal listener ({{internalUrl}}), which is never published through the reverse proxy — reachable only inside the compose network or on localhost during development. No authentication: these exist for the container runtime and Prometheus.

request.description:
Reports only that the process is running — it never checks dependencies, so a database outage does not trigger a restart loop.

Response: 200 — `{ status: "ok" }`

Probes PostgreSQL and the cache concurrently under a shared timeout and reports whether this instance can serve traffic. Failure details are logged, never returned in the body — this endpoint is reachable from the network and driver errors carry hosts and credentials.

Responses:
- 200 — `{ status: "ok", checks: { "core-db": "ok", cache: "ok" }, cache: "memory"|"redis" }`
- 503 — `status: "unavailable"`, same shape, with the failing check(s) marked `failed`

Prometheus scrape endpoint. Only present when METRICS_BACKEND=prometheus (the default) — with the `log` or `none` backend this route does not exist and answers 404, on purpose: serving an empty page would tell a scraper the service is instrumented when its numbers live elsewhere.

Response: 200 — text/plain Prometheus exposition format.

Public, unauthenticated. Reports the build version stamped at compile time.

Response: 200 — `{ version: string }`
